title.value: TESA: A Task in Entity Semantic Aggregation for Abstractive Summarization
title.justification: The title is extracted from the beginning of the paper and consistently referenced throughout the document.
title.quote: "TESA: A Task in Entity Semantic Aggregation for Abstractive Summarization"

analysis.description: This paper introduces a new task and dataset, TESA, intended for evaluating models in semantic aggregation of entities, particularly in the context of abstractive summarization. The dataset includes 5.3K crowd-sourced entity aggregations for named entities like PERSON, ORGANIZATION, and LOCATION. Baseline models were built using encoder-decoder language models fine-tuned on TESA, in comparison to simpler classification methods.

type.justification: The paper presents a new dataset and models to tackle the task of entity semantic aggregation. It involves experimental comparisons and evaluations of performed tasks, which categorizes it as an empirical research.
type.quote: "We then build baseline models for generating aggregations given a tuple of entities and document context. We fine-tune on TESA an encoder-decoder language model and compare it with simpler classification methods."

name.justification: The paper focuses on entity semantic aggregation and abstractive summarization, which are key areas within Natural Language Processing.
name.quote: "...solving this task requires finding a semantic link between all the entities in the list..."

name.justification: The task defined in the paper, TESA, is fundamentally about abstractive summarization of named entities.
name.quote: "TESA directly measures the ability of summarizers to abstract at a semantic level."

name.justification: TESA is described as a task for this specific challenge within the context of summarization.
name.quote: "TESA: A Task in Entity Semantic Aggregation for Abstractive Summarization"

name.justification: BART is the encoder-decoder model used and fine-tuned as a baseline for the TESA task in a generative and discriminative manner.
name.quote: "We introduce the first models for the TESA task which are based on an encoder-decoder system pretrained for abstractive summarization, BART (Lewis et al., 2019)."

is_contributed.justification: BART itself was not contributed by this paper, it was used as an existing model for testing purposes.
is_contributed.quote: "We introduce the first models for the TESA task which are based on an encoder-decoder system pretrained for abstractive summarization, BART (Lewis et al., 2019)."

is_executed.justification: The paper involves executing BART model as it describes its fine-tuning and evaluation for the task.
is_executed.quote: "Fine-tuning BART on TESA increased its performance significantly, especially if done discriminatively."

is_compared.justification: BART is compared to other baseline models within the experimental section of the paper.
is_compared.quote: "We compared three versions of BART, which differ based on whether and how they are fine-tuned on TESA."
